records.subject: Demand to confer the Bharat Ratna on Bhai Ghanaiya Ji.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh:

I seek to highlight the extraordinary humanitarian service rendered by Bhai Ghanaiya Ji and urge the Government to honour his unparalleled contribution to humanity by conferring upon him the country?s highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna. Today, the humanitarian services of the Red Cross Society are recognised across the world for providing selfless assistance during war, disasters and suffering. However, centuries ago, the Sikh tradition had already set an extraordinary example of universal compassion. During the time of the Tenth Sikh Guru, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, when a battle was being fought, Bhai Ghanaiya Ji provided water to wounded soldiers without distinguishing between friend and foe. When a complaint was made against him, Guru Gobind Singh Ji summoned him. Bhai Ghanaiya Ji humbly explained that Guru Sahib had taught him to see the Divine presence in every human being. Therefore, wherever he looked, he saw the same form of his Guru. Deeply moved by his spirit of selfless service, Guru Gobind Singh Ji not only appreciated his noble conduct but also entrusted him with bandages and medicinal ointment to provide first aid to the injured. This stands as a timeless example of compassion, equality, universal brotherhood and humanitarian service. I therefore urge the Government to confer the Bharat Ratna upon Bhai Ghanaiya Ji and officially observe 20 September, his birth anniversary, at the national level, inspiring future generations to serve humanity without distinction.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for removal of illegal encroachments on Rivers and Water Bodies and strict implementation of NGT directions.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh:?? ?????????

     

          I seek to draw attention of the Government to the serious issue of illegal encroachments on our rivers, streams, drains, wetlands and other natural water bodies. Rivers are not merely sources of water; they are the lifelines of our civilisation, agriculture, biodiversity and environment. However, across the country, large-scale encroachments have taken place on riverbanks, floodplains, wetlands and natural drainage channels. Such illegal constructions obstruct the natural flow of water, increase the risk of floods and cause irreparable environmental damage. In Punjab also, encroachments on rivers, choes, drains and other natural water sources have severely affected the drainage of floodwaters and have adversely impacted the ecological balance. NGT has repeatedly held that floodplains and water channels cannot be subjected to illegal occupation or construction. The Tribunal has clearly observed that obstructing the natural flow of rivers is a direct assault on the environment and endangers human life and property. Our Constitution also places a solemn responsibility upon us. Article 48A directs the State to protect and improve the environment, while Article 51A(g) makes it the fundamental duty of every citizen to safeguard our natural environment.

          When a river dies, it is not just a water body that disappears; an entire ecological system collapses with it. Therefore, there is an urgent need for a nationwide movement to free our rivers and water bodies from illegal encroachments and to ensure strict compliance with NGT directives.

?????????????????? (ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for Strict Laws to Prevent Desecration of Religious Scriptures in the Country.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh: I draw attention of the Government towards the repeated incidents of desecration of sacred religious scriptures reported across the country. In India, clear national data regarding such incidents is not readily available. However, according to the statistics of the NCRB, hundreds of cases related to hurting religious sentiments are registered every year, with Punjab reporting one of the highest numbers. It has often been observed that certain mischievous and anti-social elements deliberately disregard the sanctity and dignity of religious traditions and scriptures. Through such acts, they attempt to disturb communal harmony and create unrest in society. These incidents not only bring shame to humanity but also raise serious concerns about law and order as well as the effectiveness of governance. Sacred religious scriptures are not merely books for people. They represent spiritual guidance, moral values, and the teachings of revered Gurus. Unfortunately, some selfish and conspiratorial individuals exploit vulnerable or unaware persons, tempting them with small monetary gains to carry out such disgraceful acts while they themselves remain hidden behind the scenes and attempt to divide society. Therefore,?? I urge the Government to enact a strict and effective national law to prevent the desecration of religious scriptures. Furthermore, a Special Investigation Team should be constituted to uncover the truth behind all such incidents and identify the real culprits. Those found guilty must receive the strictest punishment to ensure justice and deter such acts in the future.

?????????????????? (ENDS)

records.subject: Concern over rising cancer cases among women in Punjab.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh: I wish to draw attention to a very serious issue: the rapid increase in cancer cases among women in Punjab. This trend is deeply concerning and demands urgent action. According to information provided by the Honorable Minister in 2025 in the Rajya Sabha, approximately 2,700 women in Punjab died of cancer, which averages to eight women per day. Between 2021 and 2025, a total of 13,299 women lost their lives due to cancer. Among these, breast cancer was the leading cause with 7,186 deaths, followed by Cervix Uteri (3,502 deaths) and Ovary cancer (2,611 deaths).? Alarmingly, cancer cases are rising even among women aged 40?45, showing that this disease is no longer limited to old age, but increasingly threatening younger lives. Environmental factors, particularly water pollution and the widespread use of chemical fertilizers in agriculture, are considered major contributors. These chemicals, once in the soil, eventually enter our food chain. The rise in cancer among women is deeply troubling. Therefore, I urge the government to ensure that: 1. Cancer treatment for women is made fully free; and 2. A subsidy of up to 50% is provided for economically weaker sections, whether the treatment is availed in government or private hospitals, so that no woman is denied care. ???????????? Women are the backbone of our society, and their health and safety are crucial for the well-being of Punjab.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for providing government assistance for transporting the mortal remains of Indian Citizens from airports to their homes.
Demand for the inclusion of Environmental Studies as a mandatory subject in every school curriculum.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh: The bond between humanity and the Earth, the planet we inhabit, is ancient and profound. Across all our religions, great respect is shown for the elements of nature?air, water, and earth. Gurbani says, ?Pavan Guru, Pani Pita, Mata DharatMahat? (That mean air is the teacher, water is the father, and the earth is the great mother). Due to the increase in global warming, we are witnessing a direct impact on humans, animals, birds, aquatic life, and plants on Earth. Disastrous floods, severe droughts, and massive storms are all a result of climate change. These changes have occurred because humans have interfered with nature on a large scale.The only solution to preventing the calamities arising from these drastic changes is to raise awareness about the environment and make it a mandatory subject in educational institutions. If we focus on addressing global changes starting from our primary schools, future generations will become passionate environmental advocates and the biggest strength of society. This is why it is said, ?Think globally, act locally.? I demand from the Government that environmental studies be made a mandatory subject in all schools in India, where children will not only learn theoretical knowledge but also hands-on lessons such as planting trees, caring for plants, conserving water, and living harmoniously with nature.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Concern over increasing Cancer cases in India.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh: Through this House, we would like to inform that cancer is currently spreading rapidly in India. According to the report of the National Cancer Registry Program under the Indian Council of Medical Research, more than 1.4 million new cases were estimated in the year 2022. According to media reports, 4109 people are getting infected with cancer every day in the country. This figure points to a dangerous trend because the number of patients falling victim to cancer is increasing rapidly every year. Punjab, which is also known as the strong arm of the country, the youth and farmers of Punjab are making a big contribution to the protection and development of the country. Even in thehealthy state of Punjab, the number of people falling victim to cancer has now reached 105 per person per day. Now Cancer has started affecting the lives of young children, animals and birds. The government is providing financial assistance for the prevention of cancer, but it is insufficient. Because its treatment is very expensive. The death of a patient due to lack of treatment or lack of money raises questions about health facilities. In the year 2021, Cancer has been said to be the cause of death of about 7 lakh 90 people and in the year 2022, about 9 lakh people. I strongly demand from the Central Government that complete treatment of cancer patients should be provided free of cost so that the hardworking people of the country can be saved from dying.

 

(ENDS)

records.subject: Regarding making Punjab free from paddy (I will speak in Punjabi)
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh: Punjab which fed the people of the country during the Green Revolution period and filled the countrys granary is currently paying a heavy price. The excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides in Punjab has turned the prosperous state into a cancer zone.

Farmers of Punjab are stuck in crop cycle of wheat and paddy. The government adopted the Minimum Support Price (MSP) policy to meet the central grain storage requirements? on the farmers of Punjab since 1973. Now every year the area under paddy is increasing in Punjab. Due to this, the pressure on the underground water is also increasing. During paddy cultivation, where the vast water storage is being affected, handling of the paddy stubble afterwards also remains a major challenge every year. Every year, precious lives are lost due to accidents due to this smoke.

Therefore, the paddy crop is not suitable according to the climatic conditions of Punjab. Pond-irrigation is required for the paddy crop, which has led to dangerous groundwater depletion in more than three-fourth blocks in Punjab. Now in Punjab, there is no life without submersible motors for irrigation of crops. These tools have become the cause of debt for the farmers. I urge the Government to take suitable measures to stop the cultivation of paddy in Punjab.

(Ends)

records.subject: Regarding compensation for horticultural crops damaged due to natural calamities (I will speak in Punjabi)
records.SM_Text:
Sant Balbir Singh: Compensation is provided by the government in cases of loss of crops due to natural calamities. These natural disasters occur frequently in the forms of floods and droughts. While horticulture also suffers losses due to natural calamities, no compensation is provided for them. Horticulture, which is also seen as an alternative form of agriculture, conserves groundwater and helps in keeping the environment clean. Orange orchards have been planted on a large scale in Fazilka, Abohar, Hoshiarpur, and other places in Punjab. After falling prey to the natural blight, many horticultural farmers repented of it and were forced to dig up their green gardens. Horticulture in this area is dependent on canal water as their groundwater is saline. This is also causing damage to the gardens. During the last two years, 2021-22 and 2022-23, around 40,000 farmers in Bathinda, Muktsar, and Fazilka uprooted their gardens due to climate change. Sir, climate change is having the worst impact on horticulture. Therefore, it is our strong demand that the interests of horticulture farmers across the country, including Punjab, should be taken care of. Sir, I request Government that in case of loss of their horticulture due to natural calamities, they should be compensated like loss of normal crops. To encourage horticulture, maximum subsidies should be given so that farmers turn to horticulture and arrange for the marketing of their fruits. Loans of horticultural farmers and laborers should be waived. Tools and machinery used for horticulture should be made cheaper.

 

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for mandatory BLS technique training in academic institutions to reduce sudden cardiac arrest death rate.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sant Balbir Singh: I would like to bring to the attention of the House through you that according to a study the death rate in the country is one crore annually, which means that every year one crore people die in one form or other. A tenth of this means that one million deaths are due to sudden cardiac arrest alone.

 

According to cardiologist, the first 3 to 10 minutes are very critical for the patient at the time of sudden cardiac arrest. According to Doctors, 3 lakh 50 out of 10 lakh deaths could be saved if the bystanders pumped the victims chest with both hands in a specific manner within these first three minutes. This technique is called BLS i.e. Basic Life Support.

 

According to a survey, only less than 0.1 percent of people know about this technique. Whereas every citizen of the country should be aware of it and be trained in it. So, if the training of this technique is made compulsory in schools, then many peoples lives can be saved.

 

I demand from the Government that training in this BLS technique should be made mandatory in schools across the country and this training should be made a part of education so that precious lives of people can be saved.

 

(Ends)

records.subject: Concern over Exploitation of Women of Country, especially women of Punjab, in Gulf Countries
records.SM_Text:
SHRI SANT BALBIR SINGH (Punjab):? Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, through you, we wish to draw the attention of the House to the serious issue that women/ girls are being taken to Gulf countries through travel agents and sold there.? Through our efforts and with the support of the Indian Embassy, we have brought back to India around 60 women from Gulf countries who were trafficked there.? Travel agents are trapping very young women/ girls from poor households and sending them on Visitor Visas to Gulf countries where they are being exploited.? They are tricked into working in homes or in restaurants and falsely assured of salaries of Rs. 35,000 to 40,000.? Then, those women are made to sign an agreement written in Arabic language, which is being taken undue advantage of.? It is a large group of people whose network is spread across different states of the country.? The girls who returned said that there were also women from Nepal, which proves that this gang is international.? It is surprising that these women are being sent to a country like Iraq, where it is very difficult to go.? We thank the Indian embassies in the Gulf countries that have helped to evacuate the distressed citizens in those countries.

????????? Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, through you, we request the Ministry of External Affairs to keep a watch on the activities of people involved in this fraudulent business and to give severe punishment to those travel agents who are involved in trafficking women.

(Ends)

records.subject: Concern over impact of air pollution on human health and need to reduce the air pollution in the country.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI SANT BALBIR SINGH (Punjab): "Sir, I would like to draw your attention to 25 per cent of cancer patients in India whose main cause is air pollution. On an average, 3 out of 4 cancer patients die because they cannot afford treatment. According to a report of 2017, twelve lakh deaths were caused by air pollution, which was 12.5 per cent of the total deaths in India. Twenty-eight per cent of people are suffering from lung cancer due to air pollution. The most harmful impact of air pollution is seen on our upcoming generation. New-born children are being born with disabilities and they have lack of mental development. According to the report of the Lancet Study 2019, 16 lakh deaths, out of 23 lakh unnatural deaths in India during 2019, were caused by air pollution and five lakh people died due to water pollution. This is the highest number of deaths due to air pollution in the country. The Central Pollution Control Board has released a list of 131 cities in India as non-attainment cities, that is, those where the air has not been breathable during last five years.

According to the Indian Constitution, clean air, water, and food are the fundamental rights of every citizen and rules are made, but despite it many deaths are caused by pollution every year.

I urge upon the Government to take necessary steps to reduce air pollution."

(Ends)

records.subject: Concern over mismanagement of water supply in the country.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI SANT BALBIR SINGH (Punjab): * "Sir, in the National Policy, drinking water supply in cities is fixed at 135 litres per capita per day, based on which treatment plants designs are prepared. But in reality, this supply is from 250 litres to 300 litres due to which the treatment plants fail. This is the case with almost all the treatment plants in the country. Crores of rupees spent on treatment plants are also going in vain. So, our demand is that drinking water should be available to all and the Central Government should fulfill its responsibility on a priority basis. Water supply in cities at the rate of 135 litres per capita should be strictly implemented so that treatment plants will not fail and untreated water being dumped into rivers will be stopped. The whole country is already facing drinking water crisis. So, the wastage of water should be stopped."

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for de-silting of river beds falling under railway bridges in Punjab.
records.SM_Text:
SANT BALBIR SINGH (Punjab): Mr. Chairman, Sir, the spans of railway bridges on rivers have got choked due to accumulation of sand and silt. This leads to stoppage of passage of water and breaches the Dhussi Bandh, resulting in floods. A peculiar case is that of the railway bridge near village Gidderpindi on the Jalandhar Ferozepur railway section, which has about 21 spans, out of which only 3 to 4 were clear and rest were choked due to accumulation of sand and silt.? Sir, as an area of 1,200 ft on upstream side and 800 ft on the downstream side fall under the jurisdiction of Railways, the main problem in the process of de-silting is the illegal occupants of land, who are opposing it tooth and nail. They are using the land falling under railway jurisdiction for cultivation and only railways can get it vacated and cleaned. As per law, cultivation is not permitted on this land as it is meant for the smooth flow of river under the railway bridge. Because of the choking of these about 17 to 18 spans, there was a massive flood in Sutlej river during the monsoon of 2019 in the area, which resulted in an approximate loss of State property worth Rs. 200 crores. It also resulted in loss of crops, livestock and homes of the people amounting to approximately Rs. 1,000 crores. The floods of 1985, 1988, 1995 and 2008 were also caused due to similar reasons. The Railway department should take steps to avoid any breach in Dhussi bandh in future.

(Ends)
